title: Fix pkill -i kills CLI processes during GUI app restart
description: restartGuiApp uses 'pgrep -ix' and 'pkill -ix' with case-insensitive flag. For Claude.app this matches both 'Claude' (desktop app) and 'claude' (CLI binary). Sequence: AppleScript quit succeeds, but pgrep still sees claude CLI procs, loop times out, pkill kills all claude CLI processes. Fix: drop -i flag (use case-sensitive exact match) or match against full executable path.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #14 — restart targets specific PIDs and uses case-sensitive launch check

title: Post-upgrade quarantine detection for never-approved executables
description:
brew-bouncer's quarantine snapshot filters to 'previously approved' (not quarantined) executables. claude-code's claude binary ships quarantined and the cask never removes it, so the snapshot records nothing, and the binary stays quarantined after every upgrade.

Fix: replace pre-approval tracking with post-upgrade quarantine detection. Enumerate executable paths upfront (no quarantine filter), then check quarantine status *after* each package upgrade and offer to remove per policy.

Files: src/quarantine.ts, src/commands/upgrade.ts, src/prompt.ts
close_reason: Replaced pre-approval snapshot with post-upgrade quarantine detection. enumeratePackageExecutables() enumerates all executable paths (no quarantine filter), then after each upgrade isQuarantined() is called post-upgrade. Handles packages like claude-code where the binary ships quarantined and was never manually approved.

title: Sequential per-package upgrade with inline restart prompts
description:
Current flow: upgrade ALL packages in one brew upgrade call, then detect and prompt for restarts at the end. This is fragile — if anything goes wrong mid-upgrade (spinner breaks, Ctrl+C needed), user loses track of what was upgraded and what needs restarting.

Proposed flow:
1. Show preview table and confirm (existing)
2. Upgrade packages ONE AT A TIME
3. After each package: show caveats, detect if it's running, prompt restart (y/N/all)
4. 'all' option skips remaining prompts and does batch upgrade+restart for the rest
5. Track progress so if interrupted, user can see what was done

This makes the tool resilient to interruption and gives better per-package feedback. The current batch approach has caused Jason to abort 3x with half-upgraded packages and no restart tracking.

Files: src/commands/upgrade.ts (main orchestration), src/brew/runner.ts (brewUpgrade)

title: Restart each .app bundle independently for multi-.app casks
description:
Some Homebrew casks declare multiple .app artifacts (e.g. wireshark ships both Wireshark.app and helper apps). Today detectRunningUpgrades aggregates matched bundles into a single DetectedApp and filters PIDs to the primary bundle's set (Option A quick win from PR #14 CodeRabbit feedback). Sibling bundles are detected but not restarted.

Follow-up: push N DetectedApps per cask (one per matched .app bundle), update upgrade.ts detectedMap from Map<packageName, DetectedApp> to multi-value, adjust the restart loop and renderPackageTable.

Why: cask with multiple matching .app bundles only primary's PIDs retained; sibling bundles dropped.

Acceptance: cask with 2+ running .app bundles all restart on upgrade; single-bundle casks behave identically; display table reasonable for multi-bundle case.
notes: Filed as follow-up to PR #14 CodeRabbit review (Option A applied as quick win, Option B deferred).

title: Restart each .app bundle independently for multi-.app casks
description:
Some Homebrew casks declare multiple `.app` artifacts (e.g. `wireshark` ships
both `Wireshark.app` and helper apps; some IDE casks include companion tools).
Currently `detectRunningUpgrades` aggregates all matched bundles into a single
`DetectedApp`, then filters PIDs to the primary bundle's set (after CodeRabbit
follow-up in fix/gui-restart-pid-targeting). Sibling bundles are detected but
not restarted.

For multi-`.app` casks where the user has more than one bundle running, we
should restart each independently rather than only the primary.

This is a follow-up to the Option A "quick win" applied for PR #14
(brew-bouncer-2vh / CodeRabbit major finding on src/detect/matcher.ts:120-137).
The CR review acknowledged the limitation: "the restart layer can only target
one displayName/bundlePath".

Why this issue exists:
- Today: cask with multiple matching .app bundles → only primary's PIDs
  retained; sibling bundles' PIDs are dropped. Sibling apps don't auto-restart.
- Want: each matched bundle becomes its own restart target.

What needs to be done:
- Change `detectRunningUpgrades` (src/detect/matcher.ts) to push N
  `DetectedApp` entries per cask, one per matched `.app` bundle.
- Update `upgrade.ts` `detectedMap` from `Map<packageName, DetectedApp>` to a
  multi-value structure (`Map<packageName, DetectedApp[]>` or list).
- Adjust the restart loop in `upgrade.ts` step 8 to iterate all DetectedApps
  per package and restart each.
- Adjust `renderPackageTable` and the affectedCount calculation to handle the
  new shape.
- Decide UX: per-bundle restart prompt or single confirm-all per cask.

Acceptance:
- Cask with 2+ running `.app` bundles → all restart on upgrade.
- Single-bundle casks behave identically to today.
- Display table reasonable for multi-bundle case.
notes: Filed as follow-up to PR #14 CodeRabbit review (Option A applied as quick win).

title: Restore interactive terminal behavior in execStreaming
description: Review feedback flagged that execStreaming switched brew stdout/stderr to pipes, which can make Homebrew think it is not attached to a TTY and suppress prompts, progress, or caveats. Verify the current implementation and restore terminal inheritance if the finding is valid.

title: Summarize brew warnings and errors after upgrade run
description: Users need an end-of-run recap of warnings and especially errors emitted during per-package brew upgrades so they do not need to scroll back through terminal output. Capture warning/error lines per package while preserving live brew passthrough, then print a compact summary after the run completes.

title: Quarantine handling only covers GUI apps, needs to cover all executables
description:
## What

brew-bouncer's quarantine snapshot/restore only looks at cask `app` artifacts (`.app` bundles in `/Applications`). CLI casks (`binary` artifacts like `claude-code`) and pkg-installed casks are never checked, and formulae are not checked at all.

## Why

CLI binaries trigger the same Gatekeeper "downloaded from internet, are you sure?" prompt as GUI apps when executed for the first time. If a user previously approved a CLI binary (removed the `com.apple.quarantine` xattr), the approval is wiped on upgrade and not re-applied — they get the prompt again on next invocation.

The scope was incorrectly narrowed to GUI apps based on a wrong assumption that only GUI apps show the quarantine dialog.

## Where

- `src/quarantine.ts:92` — `snapshotCaskQuarantine` only accepts cask info and walks `extractCaskAppNames`
- `src/brew/parser.ts:162` — `extractCaskAppNames` only returns `.app` artifacts
- `src/brew/parser.ts:180` — `extractCaskBinaryNames` exists but isn't used by quarantine
- `src/commands/upgrade.ts:138-154` — cask-only quarantine snapshot step

## How

1. Extend quarantine snapshot to cover:
   - Cask `binary` artifacts (resolve to actual install paths, typically under `/opt/homebrew/bin` or wherever brew symlinks go — need to check the real file, not the symlink)
   - Cask `pkg` installs (use `extractCaskPkgIds` + `pkgutil --only-files --files <id>` to enumerate installed files, then filter to executables)
   - Formulae (walk `brew --prefix/Cellar/<name>/<ver>/bin` for installed binaries)
2. `isQuarantined` / `removeQuarantine` already work on any path — no changes needed there
3. Update `snapshotCaskQuarantine` signature to take both casks and formulae, or add a parallel `snapshotFormulaQuarantine`
4. Update upgrade.ts to run snapshot for all package types

## Affected hosts/environments

macOS only. Quarantine is a macOS Gatekeeper feature.
notes: PR opened: https://github.com/jdillon/brew-bouncer/pull/9 (commit e9ec855). Covers cask app/binary/pkg artifacts and formula binaries. pkg path resolution still assumes /Applications — non-standard install locations would need a follow-up.

title: Normalize prompt styles across all user interactions
description:
Current prompts use inconsistent formats:
- Upgrade: `Proceed with upgrade? [Y/n/select]`
- Restart: `Restart 3 affected app(s) after upgrade? [yes / ask each / No]`
- Quarantine: `Remove quarantine from 1 previously-approved app(s) after upgrade? [yes / No / ask]`

These should follow a consistent pattern for key bindings, capitalization (default indicator), spacing, and option ordering. Audit all prompts in src/prompt.ts and standardize.

title: Enhance GUI app restart to poll for quit completion
description: restartGuiApp uses a fixed 1500ms sleep after sending osascript quit, which isn't enough for slow-to-quit apps like Claude Desktop. Need to poll for process termination, escalate with SIGTERM if graceful quit stalls, and handle reopen more robustly.
close_reason: Replaced fixed 1500ms sleep with poll-based quit detection. Now polls pgrep -ix every 500ms for up to 10s, escalates to pkill SIGTERM if graceful quit stalls, and fails cleanly if app won't terminate. Fast-quitting apps restart faster, slow-quitting apps like Claude Desktop actually work.

title: Caveat extraction from brew output stream is broken
description:
The execTee caveat handling has multiple issues:
1. CAVEAT_END regex (^==>) matches any section header, ending the caveat block prematurely if brew interleaves output
2. Caveat header regex (^==> Caveats$) doesn't match per-package form (==> Caveats for docker)
3. Caveat body lines are collected in importantLines but never surfaced via onLine during upgrade
4. The ==> Caveats header calls onLine which sets spinner detail to '==> Caveats' — not useful
5. Long warning lines (e.g. docker-completion conflict ~150 chars) were breaking spinner by wrapping past terminal width (fixed: spinner now truncates)

Files: src/brew/runner.ts:100-153 (execTee caveat/important line handling)
